info.title: ProxyShop exchange
info.description: The pinned exchange routes of DESIGN §Interfaces. Every request and response body carries a checked-in example, and `tests/test_openapi_contracts.py` / `tests/openapi.test.ts` validate each example against the protocol schema it names. That is what makes these examples a contract rather than documentation: an example that stops matching the schema fails the build in both languages.

get.summary: Read one auction's state, its transitions and the bid it accepted.
get.description: The auction-state read a client polls after `POST /auctions` and `POST /auctions/{auction_id}/accept`; `proxyshop_demo/s1.py` drives it over HTTP twice. It was SERVED and declared nowhere (T-266, T-312) — a live, unauthenticated read of auction state that no generated client could reach and no contract review had ever seen. Declared here so both are false.

200.description: The auction as the store holds it, with every state transition it made.

404.description: The auction was never created, or its 900s TTL has expired.

post.summary: Accept one shortlisted bid and receive the exchange-minted permalink.
post.description: Reaches checkout through the injected CheckoutProvider port, never a hard-wired merchant call. Eligibility is RE-READ here (R12/D54), so a store blacklisted after it bid gets no code and no permalink.

200.description: Accepted; the buyer follows this permalink and never mints its own.

409.description: Denied at the checkout eligibility gate.

denial_reason.description: A declared refusal code, then either the end of the string or a colon followed by free diagnostic prose. Parse only the token before the first colon; everything after it is for a human and is not part of the contract. The nine codes are published as the enum `protocol.schema.json#/$defs/DenialCode` — a typed vocabulary in both generated languages, and `contracts/ts/vocabulary.ts` carries the runtime list `DENIAL_CODES` plus `denialCode(reason)`, the parser this paragraph describes. Use it: `split(':')[0].trim()` disagrees with the exchange on U+001C-U+001F, which Python's `str.strip()` removes and JavaScript's `trim()` keeps. A refusal whose code this exchange does not declare is re-published as `unspecified` with its prose intact, so a client never sees a tenth token. The exchange writes the separator `": "` itself, but it also forwards a refusal VERBATIM when the reason a seller-eligibility source handed it already begins with a declared code, and the parser that decides that (`reasons.denial_code`) splits on a bare `":"` and strips the token — so `blacklisted:no space`, `blacklisted : x` and a bare `blacklisted:` are all values this endpoint really returns, and the pattern admits them. The run of blanks before the colon is spelled out by code point rather than as `\s`, which means three different sets to Python, Rust and ECMAScript and would make this one constraint mean three things (T-115). NOT an `enum` on THIS field, and that is measured rather than assumed: a booted exchange driven over HTTP answered "unknown_bid: auction '…' carries no bid '…'; there is nothing to accept", "blacklisted: chargeback fraud" and "checkout_refused: RuntimeError: merchant declined to mint", so an `enum` of the bare codes would be a published constraint essentially every real 409 violates. The enumeration therefore lives on the CODE and this field keeps the `pattern`. T-204 CLOSED: the service now publishes that bare code as `denial_code` beside this field — `routes._denied` already computed it (it is how an undeclared reason is republished as `unspecified`) and threw it away — so the vocabulary is an `enum` on a field whose every served value is a member of it, rather than an `enum` on this one, which essentially every real 409 would violate. Branch on `denial_code`; read this field for the diagnosis.

denial_code.description: The bare declared code for this refusal, and the field a client branches on. Always one of the nine values enumerated here — `routes._denied` republishes a reason it does not recognise under `unspecified` rather than letting an undeclared token reach a client — so unlike `denial_reason` this property can carry a true `enum`, which is what closed T-204. It is the SAME vocabulary as `protocol.schema.json#/$defs/DenialCode`, generated into Python and TypeScript, and `contracts/ts/vocabulary.ts` publishes the runtime list as `DENIAL_CODES`. Prefer it over parsing `denial_reason`: the split-on-colon parser that field's description describes disagrees with the exchange on U+001C-U+001F, which Python strips and JavaScript's `trim()` keeps, and a consumer that never has to parse cannot get that wrong.

post.summary: The signed external door: a Tier-2 seller submits a Bid.
post.description: D52: the SigningEnvelope is REQUIRED. A submission missing any one of signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce or schema_version is Rejected before extraction and before verification, with the same finality as a bad signature. There is no legacy-tolerant path.

example.message: Warmest merino mid-layer on the market.

202.description: AcceptedForVerification. Admitted is not trusted: the seller_asserted claims are queued for verification (R18).

400.description: Rejected. Each rejection is final — never a downgrade to admitted-unverified.

post.summary: Trust reports an outcome back to the exchange for the bandit update.

get.summary: One merchant's own aggregated win/loss report over a window (R9).
get.description: Served by `exchange.reports.routes` and fed by a real producer: `POST /auctions` writes one loss row per candidate at close (`reports.log.record_losses`), and this door reads back only the rows whose SUBJECT is the calling store. The store is resolved FROM the bearer token — the table is `{store_id: token}` — so there is no path, query or body field in which to ask for another merchant's losses, and every row is compared with `hmac.compare_digest` so the time taken says nothing about which token was presented. A deployment that has not named `report_tokens_file` in its composition document holds no table and serves nobody (503) rather than opening itself the moment the environment is incomplete. The body carries reason categories and unmet buyer criteria only — no rival identity and no amount — enforced by `reports.loss.build_loss_report`'s projection rather than by a list of forbidden field names, and re-checked by that function's egress scan, which refuses the response with a 500 carrying nothing from the report rather than shipping a body holding a value the projection never read. R9's merchant dashboard does not exist in this repository yet; this is the published URL it, a merchant's own script, or `curl` reaches.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: `Bearer <this store's report token>`. The token IS the store identity — the exchange resolves the subject store from it — which is why this operation declares no `store_id` parameter of any kind. A request with no bearer, or one carrying a token in no row of the table, is refused 401 without naming a store and without echoing what arrived.

200.description: This store's own losses, aggregated by intent cluster. A store that lost nothing in the window is served an empty `by_cluster`, not a 404: "you lost nothing" is an answer, and a 404 would be indistinguishable from a store the exchange has never heard of.

400.description: The window itself does not read — `end` before `start`, or a NaN bound. A malformed ROW is the exchange's own fault and is a 500 rather than a 400 dressed up as one.

401.description: No bearer, or a bearer in no row of the token table. Names no store and echoes nothing that arrived: a refusal quoting the presented token would put it in every proxy log between here and the caller.

503.description: This exchange holds no report token table, so it serves no merchant its losses. An empty expected value compared against an empty supplied one is a route that opens itself when the environment is incomplete, so an unconfigured deployment refuses every caller instead.

example.detail: this exchange holds no report token table, so it serves no merchant its losses. State `report_tokens_file` in the deployment document
